title: Gabber upstairs relation with tensor coefficients
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, with B a finite A-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let I be an ideal of A contained in its Jacobson radical. Let B_1 and B_2 be A/I-algebras and let e: B/IB ≃ B_1 × B_2 be a ring equivalence compatible with the A/I structure maps. Assume A/I → B_1 is surjective and b in B maps to (1,0). There exist a commutative A-algebra C in the universe of A, faithfully flat over A, a positive integer d, and c_j in C tensor_A I for j in Fin(d+1), such that 1 tensor ((b-1)b^d) equals the sum of the images of c_j under the base changes of the A-linear maps I → B, i ↦ i*b^j. This is an equality in C tensor_A B, before taking a quotient.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290) and its proof (uses Lemma 07M4 lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs, Nakayama Algebra Lemma 00DV lemma-NAK, Algebra Lemma 00H5 lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal, and faithful flatness of the etale A -> A' whose image contains V(I): Algebra Lemma 05CK lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective, Proposition 00I1 proposition-fppf-open); Stacks writes the hypothesis as 'A/I -> B_1/IB_1 surjective', where B_1 is already an A/I-algebra, so B_1/IB_1 = B_1

proof.text: Apply the flat split neighbourhood theorem to obtain C, the quotient compatibility, ideals K and L, and the first and second factor relations.
Use the quotient compatibility and the Jacobson radical hypothesis with the flat maximal-fibre criterion to prove C is faithfully flat over A.

In the quotient by L, apply the monic polynomial annihilator for an element of an extended ideal. Multiply by X and then by X - 1 - a; the zero intersection K ⊓ L gives a relation whose difference from (X - 1)X^d has coefficients in IC.
Represent each coefficient in IC by a tensor in C tensor_A I using span induction, evaluate the resulting coefficient tensors, and identify the left side via the tensor algebra map.

lean.statement: theorem exists_gabber_upstairs_tensor_relation {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥) (B₁ : Type w) (B₂ : Type z) [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₁] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₂] (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃+* (B₁ × B₂)) (he : ∀ a : A, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B a)) = (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₁ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a), algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₂ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a))) (h₁ : Function.Surjective (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₁)) (b : B) (hb : e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b) = (1, 0)) : ∃ (C : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : A →+* C), letI : Algebra A C := f.toAlgebra Module.FaithfullyFlat A C ∧ ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ ∃ c : Fin (d + 1) → TensorProduct A C I, TensorProduct.tmul A (1 : C) ((b - 1) * b ^ d) = ∑ j : Fin (d + 1), (I.subtype.smulRight (b ^ (j : ℕ))).lTensor C (c j)
